column2: Software Development using AI
UG

This course examines modern AI-native software development, where developers collaborate with coding agents. It covers how to define intent, provide effective context, structure development workflows, and coordinate AI tools. Students gain practical experience designing and evaluating agent-assisted software development processes. The course matters for target students by equipping them with practical skills in agentic development environments, tool use and orchestration frameworks, specification-driven development, loop engineering and execution traces, testing, evaluation, and reliability, as well as a capstone project. Students will be able to configure coding assistants, implement agent skills and tool use integrations, construct executable specifications, analyse loop engineering execution traces, evaluate reliability and automated test coverage, and assess end-to-end AI-native software development projects. The course is taught through lectures, tutorials, and laboratory sessions involving hands-on coding and projects.

CO2

Course Code: Configure coding assistants and developer workflows for a given software task, using an agentic development environment, such that at least 80% of the provided test cases pass.
column2: Implement agent skills and tool use integrations within an orchestration framework, given an API specification, meeting the stated interface specification for every public method.
column3: Construct executable specifications from natural language requirements using a spec-driven development tool, covering every use case in the supplied requirements document.
column4: Analyse loop engineering execution traces from a coding agent run, identifying at least three distinct failure causes with supporting log evidence.
column5: Evaluate the reliability and automated test coverage of an AI-generated software artifact, justifying each validation choice against at least one stated requirement.
column6: Evaluate an end-to-end AI-native software development project incorporating coding agents and automated workflows, justifying each design decision against at least one stated requirement.
